messages:
sara_support: customer: we're seeing very high p99 on requests that should route to us-west. they report tokens billed in eu-west and 200-300ms extra latency. request id example: req_0a1b2c3d. they claim they set X-Client-Region: us-west but traces show eu host. any ideas?

acme-sre: adding some headers they sent (redacted):
```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Client-Region: us-west
X-Client-Region: eu-west
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
```
They said their proxy adds a header, but their SDK also sets one as a query param: `?region=us-west`. Not sure how both ended up in the request.

ivan_infra: hmm two X-Client-Region headers present. our router should take the first header and then query param if header missing. can you paste the exact raw request (tcp capture) or a curl that reproduces this? also which SDK version?

acme-sre: repro curl we used locally: 
```
curl -v -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" -H "X-Client-Region: us-west" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-west" \n -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED"
```
When both headers present the traffic goes to eu. when we remove the eu-west header it goes to us.

ivan_infra: thanks. that suggests header-order precedence bug. sending to @elliot_eng for confirmation. tagging deploy-bot: did anything change in routing precedence in last 24h?

deploy-bot: deploy: routing-service v1.38.0 rolled out 2025-11-12T02:13:07Z (sha: a1b2c3).

elliot_eng: I can repro locally with that curl. looks like a recent optimization that dedupes headers ended up using last-seen header value instead of first. so for duplicate X-Client-Region we pick the last one (eu-west in your example) which flips precedence. previously we consistently used the first header. query param logic still prefers header over param, but because we read last header, behavior changed.

elliot_eng: short-term mitigation: remove the duplicate header on the client/proxy. we can also add a guard in routing-service config to treat multiple X-Client-Region as ambiguous and prefer first-seen. I'll push a hotfix to revert the dedupe behavior.

acme-sre: we pushed a quick proxy rule to drop duplicate X-Client-Region and that restored routing to us-west. thanks.

ivan_infra: can you provide logs for req_0a1b2c3d? we want to confirm which node received it and the header list.

acme-sre: attached log snippet (sanitized):
```
[1769123456] req_0a1b2c3d host=eu-west-1.rw node=n1 headers="X-Client-Region: eu-west; X-Client-Region: us-west; region=us-west"
```
Shows last header as eu-west.

elliot_eng: confirmed. plan: 
1) immediate: patch routing-service to prefer first-seen header (rollout in 30m)
2) follow-up: add warning metric for duplicate region headers and a consumer-facing doc blurb (SDKs should not send header+param or duplicate headers)
3) postmortem in eng channel with RCA and timeline.

ivan_infra: ETA for patch?

elliot_eng: patch ready, running canary now (10% nodes). will monitor routing success and token billing, will promote to 100% if green.

acme-sre: can you also confirm any billing corrections for affected requests? our finance team flagged a batch.

elliot_eng: we'll capture the affected request IDs and coordinate with billing. please DM the list or paste the req ids you saw.

acme-sre: pasted a short list in DM. thanks.

sara_support: marking this as escalated -> eng oncall. updating the customer: temporary workaround (remove duplicate header or disable proxy header injection). ETA for full fix ~45m. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout: routing-service v1.38.1 canary -> success metrics ok, 100% rollout started.

elliot_eng: 100% rolled out. monitoring shows routing matches header-first semantics again. closing loop with billing and docs.

acme-sre: confirmed their traffic is now routing to us-west and latency is back to normal. thanks all! :party:
